summary.headline: Hester Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 22% and PAT 174% YoY; FY26 consolidated PAT nearly doubled on 7% revenue growth.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 standalone revenue up 22% and PAT up 174%, with full-year standalone revenue flat but PAT up 64%. Consolidated revenue grew 22% in Q4 and 7% for FY26, with full-year PAT almost doubling, partly aided by an exceptional gain from the partial divestment of Texas Lifesciences. Poultry Healthcare led growth (+41% in Q4, +21% for FY26), while Animal Healthcare lagged on tender delays. Management said Animal Healthcare demand is intact and expects recovery from Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: Almost doubled (~100%) YoY, aided by exceptional financial income
About INR 6.5 crore vs INR 2.4 crore in prior year
About INR 70 crore, down from INR 102 crore
About INR 92 crore on revenue below INR 300 crore (as cited by analyst)

segments.name: Poultry Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 41% in Q4 and 21% for FY26, driven by deeper penetration, expanded placements and vaccine demand. Analyst cited record quarterly poultry revenue near INR 65 crore with margins near 30%; management did not confirm the figure and said it aims to sustain the level.

segments.name: Animal Healthcare (India)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell about 30% YoY per analyst, due to delayed tender-led immunisation programmes. National PPR programme execution improved in Q4, with 6.3 crore PPR doses supplied in the quarter.

segments.name: Africa / International
segments.commentary: Participating in GALVmed-led VITAL 2 programme and expanding registrations across key African markets. Competition is three or four private animal vaccine producers. Vaccines invoiced in USD for export countries and in local currency domestically.

segments.name: Petcare
segments.commentary: Scaling gradually in selected therapeutic and supplement products. No commercialised pet vaccines yet, so no share in pet vaccination.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Animal Healthcare to recover from Q1 FY27 onward, after a year of tender delays.
Aim to avoid over-dependence on one division; poultry/animal split was near 50:50 two years ago and FY26 skewed toward poultry (about 70:30).
Management intends to sustain poultry profitability levels seen in Q4 but gave no numerical guidance.
Focus for FY27 is disciplined growth, operational efficiency, receivables reduction and BSL-3 utilisation.
No firm commitment on further capex; regulatory changes may require future investment.
capex_capacity: Fill-Finish and BSL-3 facilities capitalised during the year; Fill-Finish expands drug product capacity for domestic and export markets.
BSL-3 facility under optimisation to improve utilisation and operating cost; management said it is working to fully utilise the facility.
Received marketing and manufacturing licences for H9N2 Avian Influenza vaccine in Q4 FY26.
Partial divestment of stake in Texas Lifesciences generated the exceptional item.
Nepal operations under close monitoring for operating stability.
demand_pricing: Poultry demand supported by vaccine portfolio, field execution and possibly high broiler prices in Q4 (analyst view; not confirmed by management).
Raw material costs rising due to global geopolitical developments and supply-chain disruptions; management may calibrate price actions.
Tender timing volatility continues to hit Animal Healthcare; non-tender business being pushed for penetration.
Africa: VITAL 2 participation; PPR eradication demand visibility strong but timing depends on country rollouts; political disturbances in parts of the region.
Tanzania: already supplying vaccines to the government; some requested vaccines may not be in pipeline; FMD not yet being discussed.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the Tanzania livestock vaccination opportunity and who are the competitors in Africa?
qa_highlights.answer: Hester Africa already supplies vaccines for Tanzania from its local plant and is in talks with government on further vaccines. FMD is not yet under discussion. Competition is three or four private animal vaccine producers, with most governments having small state-owned units and most vaccines imported.

qa_highlights.question: Are African sales invoiced in USD or local currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports to other African countries are invoiced in USD; local sales are in local currency. Management declined to give the local versus other-country split.

qa_highlights.question: Is the high Q4 poultry revenue and ~30% margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an endeavour to continue and that the level is a base to sustain, citing product mix and bottom-line focus, but could not predict external factors.

qa_highlights.question: Why were bad debt write-offs about INR 6.5 crore, and will they fall?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it reflects provisioning on debtors plus identification and write-off of some old unrecovered debts. Management expects the figure to reduce, though not to be alarming.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables of INR 92 crore look high versus revenue; what is being done on working capital and is the new BSL-3 facility being used?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q4 sales were over 33% higher than the prior quarter, and receivable days are being worked on. Management said BSL-3 optimisation is underway to align with current needs and it is working to fully utilise it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Animal Healthcare in FY27 and will subsidiaries break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged tender delays through FY26 that did not go to plan. It said Animal Healthcare picked up from Q4 and will recover from this quarter. No subsidiary breakeven timeline was given in the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is Hester's share in pet vaccination?
qa_highlights.answer: None, as the company has no commercialised pet vaccines yet.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating leverage come as debt falls and capacity is in place, and is further capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said significant capacity is installed and utilisation will be optimised, but evolving regulatory requirements and new technologies mean future capital needs cannot be ruled out.

qa_highlights.question: What steady-state revenue mix between poultry and animal healthcare and what net debt/equity level is comfortable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aim is around 50:50, as two years ago, and FY26 skewed toward poultry. CFO said debt is about INR 70 crore (down from INR 102 crore) and debt-to-equity of 0.19x is comfortable.

risks_watch: Animal Healthcare recovery depends on tender-led programme timing, which has slipped repeatedly through FY26.
Poultry margin sustainability: Q4 strength may have been helped by high broiler prices, and FY26 profit was helped by exceptional income from the Texas Lifesciences stake sale.
Receivables are high relative to quarterly revenue and bad-debt write-offs rose to about INR 6.5 crore from INR 2.4 crore.
Raw material cost inflation linked to geopolitical and supply-chain disruptions.
Africa political disturbances and Nepal operating environment; BSL-3 facility under-utilisation and optimisation costs.
Ongoing regulatory-driven capex needs; H9N2 vaccine commercialisation and export pathway timing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on poultry and bottom-line gains, but defensive on Animal Healthcare, attributing tender delays to factors outside its control. Evasive on the Africa split, the subsidiary breakeven timeline and future capex, giving no numerical guidance.
key_quotes: While standalone revenue remained flat for the entire financial year, the profitability improved significantly with the PAT up by 64%.
These were simply timing - related challenges and no issues in the demand.
Currently, sir, the debt is around INR70 crores, right? It's reduced from INR102 crores, okay?
we are going to recover it from this quarter onwards.

adds.what: Fill-Finish facility capitalised during FY26 (drug product capacity for domestic and export markets); no size stated
H9N2 Avian Influenza vaccine marketing and manufacturing licences received in Q4 FY26 (licence, not capacity)

growth.why: Management guides only qualitatively: Animal Healthcare to recover from Q1 FY27 after tender delays and poultry profitability to be sustained, with no numerical guidance; backing is vague, with Fill-Finish and H9N2 licences as the only concrete items and no capacity size or utilisation figures given.
